newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gingrich backs fast-track authority for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich backs fast-track authority for Clinton.

text.p: Republican leaders in the U.S. Congress are firmly committed to giving President Bill Clinton "fast-track" authority to conclude trade deals, House of Representatives speaker Newt Gingrich said on Sunday.

"I am passionately committed to passing fast track. Ideally I'd like to get it thorugh in time for the president to take it with him to South America," the Georgia Republican told the annual World Economic Forum in Davos.
"There is no reason, at least from our side in the House, that we can't get fast track done. I think you will find the Republican leadership in the House and Senate actively committed to fast track."
Gingrich said he thought legislation should be modeled on the powers former President Gorge Bush had, which neither blocked the president from negotiating some items nor required him to do so.

U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said last month that, without fast-track negotiating authority, it would be difficult for the United States to get a free trade agreement with Chile, a goal of several U.S. administrations.
Fast-track authority allows a straight up-or-down vote in Congress on such deals, freeing them from amendments that could stall them.
Gingrich told a panel discussion at the meeting of business and political leaders that the Clinton administration should not abuse the authority by trying to take it too far.

"If you start dumping all sorts of social policies into your trade negotiations you are going to find it harder to reach an agrement with other countries and you may find it harder to get it approved in Congress," he said.
